AccessPolicy

subresource of Global singleton

AccessPolicy is an access policy resource nested under a parent resource (or the global singleton installation). Every parent resource has at most one access policy resource, named "default".

Methods

MethodDescriptionRequestResponse
GetGlobalAccessPolicy

Get the deployment-wide global access policy singleton. Returns NotFound until the policy has been created.

 GetGlobalAccessPolicyRequest AccessPolicy
CreateGlobalAccessPolicy

Create the deployment-wide global access policy singleton. The server's configured bootstrap owners are global owners whether or not this policy exists, so they can create it.

 CreateGlobalAccessPolicyRequest AccessPolicy
UpdateGlobalAccessPolicy

Replace the deployment-wide global access policy singleton. Empty bindings revoke every grant held through the policy; bootstrap owners keep access.

 UpdateGlobalAccessPolicyRequest AccessPolicy

Fields

metadata ResourceMetadata

Standard resource metadata. Atespace must match the parent resource (empty for global-scoped parents like Global and Atespace) and name must be "default". Both are caller-specified on create and immutable. UID, version, create_time, and update_time are server-managed.

metadata.atespace string

atespace is the namespace the resource belongs to. Empty for global-scoped resources. Caller-specified at creation and immutable thereafter.

Atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:required Non-atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:forbidden

metadata.name string

name is the resource's name, unique within its atespace (or globally, for global-scoped resources). Caller-specified at creation and immutable thereafter.

metadata.uid string

uid is a server-assigned, globally unique identifier for this resource. Immutable throughout the lifecycle of the resource.

This field is ignored during create operations and used as precondition for update operations.

metadata.version int64

version is increased on every mutation.

This field is ignored during create operations and used as precondition for update operations.

metadata.create_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

create_time is the time the resource was created.

This field is ignored on input.

metadata.update_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

update_time is the time the resource was last updated.

This field is ignored on input.

bindings repeated Binding

Role bindings granting permissions on the parent resource.

bindings.role string

The role name for the parent resource type (e.g., "owner", "editor", "viewer").

bindings.members repeated string

Principal identities granted this role. Examples:

  • "user:alice@example.com"
  • "user:sa-ci-runner"

Example

{  "metadata": {    "name": "default",    "uid": "6f7a8b9c-0d1e-4f2a-9b3c-4d5e6f7a8b9c",    "version": "4",    "createTime": "2026-06-01T00:05:00Z",    "updateTime": "2026-08-10T16:30:00Z"  },  "bindings": [    {      "role": "owner",      "members": [        "user:alice@example.com"      ]    },    {      "role": "viewer",      "members": [        "user:sa-ci-runner"      ]    }  ]}

The name of the referenced resource. This field is required.

name string

Name of the singleton access policy. Must be "default".

options DeleteOptions

Optional per-delete preconditions.

options.version int64

Delete only if the resource is still at this version, that is, unchanged since the caller read it. Zero skips the check.

options.uid string

Delete only if the resource still has this uid, that is, it is the one the caller read and not a later one created under the same name. Empty skips the check.

Actor

atespace

Subresources

  • EgressPolicy singleton

Methods

MethodDescriptionRequestResponse
GetActor

Get an Actor.

 GetActorRequest Actor
CreateActor

Create a new Actor deriving from a given ActorTemplate.

 CreateActorRequest Actor
UpdateActor

Update mutable fields on an existing Actor.

 UpdateActorRequest Actor
SuspendActor

Suspend a given actor to a new snapshot. A running actor is checkpointed on its worker; a paused actor's node-local snapshot is uploaded, narrowed to the template's commit scope where required (Full capture, Data commit).

 SuspendActorRequest SuspendActorResponse
PauseActor

Pause a given actor: checkpoint it to its worker's node and leave it SUSPENDED with that node-local snapshot, pinned to the node. A paused actor is told from a suspended one by its snapshots, not its state.

 PauseActorRequest PauseActorResponse
ResumeActor

Resume an actor from its latest snapshot.

 ResumeActorRequest ResumeActorResponse
RevertActor

Revert an actor to SUSPENDED state at its durable snapshot. Only crashed, running or paused actors can be reverted.

 RevertActorRequest RevertActorResponse
DeleteActor

Delete an actor. Only suspended or crashed actors can be deleted unless any_state is set.

 DeleteActorRequest Actor
MintActorJwt

Create a Substrate-issued JWT asserting the actor identity.

 MintActorJwtRequest MintActorJwtResponse
MintActorCertificate

Create a Substrate-issued SPIFFE certificate asserting the actor identity.

 MintActorCertificateRequest MintActorCertificateResponse
ListActors

List Actors.

 ListActorsRequest ListActorsResponse

metadata ResourceMetadata

Common resource metadata: atespace, name, uid, version, timestamps.

metadata.atespace string

atespace is the namespace the resource belongs to. Empty for global-scoped resources. Caller-specified at creation and immutable thereafter.

Atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:required Non-atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:forbidden

metadata.name string

name is the resource's name, unique within its atespace (or globally, for global-scoped resources). Caller-specified at creation and immutable thereafter.

metadata.uid string

uid is a server-assigned, globally unique identifier for this resource. Immutable throughout the lifecycle of the resource.

This field is ignored during create operations and used as precondition for update operations.

metadata.version int64

version is increased on every mutation.

This field is ignored during create operations and used as precondition for update operations.

metadata.create_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

create_time is the time the resource was created.

This field is ignored on input.

metadata.update_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

update_time is the time the resource was last updated.

This field is ignored on input.

actor_template ObjectRef

TODO: replace with full actor_template spec if we decide to make each Actor self-contained.

actor_template.atespace string

The atespace of the referenced resource. This field should be empty if the target resource is global-scoped, but references to objects in the same atespace as the referrer must still populate this field.

References to atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:required References to non-atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:forbidden

actor_template.name string

The name of the referenced resource. This field is required.

worker_selector Selector

worker_selector is the per-actor placement constraint. The scheduler evaluates the AND of this selector and the template's workerSelector to find eligible pools. Changes take effect on the next ResumeActor call.

worker_selector.match_labels map<string, string>

match_labels selects by exact equality on a set of labels.

source_tag ObjectRef

The tag specified by the caller at CreateActor to seed this Actor from an ActorSnapshot. Unset if the Actor was not created from a snapshot. Set once at creation and immutable afterward.

source_tag.atespace string

The atespace of the referenced resource. This field should be empty if the target resource is global-scoped, but references to objects in the same atespace as the referrer must still populate this field.

References to atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:required References to non-atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:forbidden

source_tag.name string

The name of the referenced resource. This field is required.

status ActorStatus

status is the system-managed state of the Actor. It is updated by the server and ignored on input. It is always present in output.

status.state ActorState

state is the Actor's current lifecycle state.

status.worker_assignment WorkerAssignment

worker_assignment points at the worker currently hosting this Actor. Unset whenever the Actor has no worker (SUSPENDED, CRASHED).

status.worker_assignment.worker ObjectRef

worker references the assigned Worker. This is the field to look the Worker up by; the worker_* fields below are a denormalized copy kept so that readers on a hot path do not have to fetch the Worker at all.

Workers are global-scoped, so this carries no atespace.

status.worker_assignment.worker.atespace string

The atespace of the referenced resource. This field should be empty if the target resource is global-scoped, but references to objects in the same atespace as the referrer must still populate this field.

References to atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:required References to non-atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:forbidden

status.worker_assignment.worker.name string

The name of the referenced resource. This field is required.

status.worker_assignment.worker_namespace string

worker_namespace is the Kubernetes namespace of the WorkerPool and worker Pod.

status.worker_assignment.worker_pool string

worker_pool is the name of the WorkerPool the worker belongs to.

status.worker_assignment.worker_pod string

worker_pod is the name of the Kubernetes pod hosting the Actor.

status.worker_assignment.worker_pod_uid string

worker_pod_uid is the Kubernetes UID of worker_pod.

status.worker_assignment.worker_pod_ips repeated string

worker_pod_ips are the IPs of worker_pod, copied from Worker.ips.

status.worker_assignment.node_name string

node_name is the Kubernetes node hosting worker_pod.

status.worker_assignment.worker_epoch int64

worker_epoch is the Worker's epoch when the Actor was placed on it. 0 if the Worker had not reported one.

status.worker_assignment.sandbox_runtime SandboxRuntime

sandbox_runtime is the sandbox runtime and compatibility version the Actor was started or restored under on this Worker.

status.worker_assignment.sandbox_runtime.sandbox_class string

e.g. "gvisor", "microvm"

status.worker_assignment.sandbox_runtime.version VersionedSandboxCompat

Primary compatibility version stamped onto an actor's snapshot when a checkpoint is taken on this runtime. Snapshots matching version can warm-boot on this runtime. TODO: Add support for additional compatibility versions.

status.worker_assignment.sandbox_runtime.version.schema_version string

Compatibility schema version (e.g. "v1") defining which runtime and hardware attributes are recorded and how they are computed.

status.worker_assignment.sandbox_runtime.version.attributes repeated AttributeEntry

Key-value compatibility attributes defined by this schema version, covering both runtime assets (e.g. "sandbox_bundle_hash") and effective guest hardware features after masking (e.g. "architecture", "cpu_features"). Matched against a snapshot under the same schema_version: every attribute on the snapshot must be present on the worker with an equal value (except "cpu_features", where the snapshot's hexadecimal bitmask must be a bitwise subset of the worker's); keys only the worker has are ignored, so a worker can gain keys under one schema_version without invalidating older snapshots. Removing or recomputing a key is a new schema_version, under which older snapshots no longer match. Order as sent does not matter: ate-api-server sorts attributes by key before recording them.

Attribute name (e.g. "architecture", "cpu_features", "sandbox_bundle_hash").

status.external_volumes repeated ExternalVolume

Volumes attached to the actor. These volumes only live as long as the actor. They are deleted when the actor is deleted. Each template volume appears at most once.

status.external_volumes.name string

Name of the volume specified in the actor template. Template volume names are DNS labels.

status.external_volumes.storage_volume_id string

The globally unique volume_id returned from the storage system. This will be initially empty during volume creation. Its format is the storage system's own, so it is only bounded and checked for control characters (U+0000-U+0008, U+000B, U+000C, U+000E-U+001F, U+007F-U+009F). The CSI spec caps IDs at 128 bytes but does not require it, so allow some slack. Set once when provisioning completes, then never changed.

status.external_volumes.volume_type string

Internal volume plugin name or CSI driver name, from the StorageClass provisioner. Must be a DNS subdomain, optionally prefixed with "substrate.io/" (per the CSI spec's driver-name syntax).

status.external_volumes.volume_context map<string, string>

volume_context contains metadata returned by the CSI driver during volume provisioning, needed by the node plugin for mounting (e.g. attachment info). Keys and values are the driver's own, so the map is only bounded, not validated.

actor.status.external_volumes repeated ExternalVolume

Name of the volume specified in the actor template. Template volume names are DNS labels.

actor.status.external_volumes.storage_volume_id string

The globally unique volume_id returned from the storage system. This will be initially empty during volume creation. Its format is the storage system's own, so it is only bounded and checked for control characters (U+0000-U+0008, U+000B, U+000C, U+000E-U+001F, U+007F-U+009F). The CSI spec caps IDs at 128 bytes but does not require it, so allow some slack. Set once when provisioning completes, then never changed.

owner identifies the origin and ownership of this snapshot.

fidelity is what this snapshot holds.

UID of the ActorTemplate whose sandbox this snapshot's guest state was captured from.

durable_snapshot holds the durable storage representation of this snapshot. Unset when the snapshot only exists locally.

object snapshot is stored in object storage.

actor.status.snapshots.sandbox_runtime.sandbox_class string

e.g. "gvisor", "microvm"

actor.status.snapshots.sandbox_runtime.version VersionedSandboxCompat

Primary compatibility version stamped onto an actor's snapshot when a checkpoint is taken on this runtime. Snapshots matching version can warm-boot on this runtime. TODO: Add support for additional compatibility versions.

actor.status.snapshots.sandbox_runtime.version.schema_version string

Compatibility schema version (e.g. "v1") defining which runtime and hardware attributes are recorded and how they are computed.

actor.status.snapshots.sandbox_runtime.version.attributes repeated AttributeEntry

Key-value compatibility attributes defined by this schema version, covering both runtime assets (e.g. "sandbox_bundle_hash") and effective guest hardware features after masking (e.g. "architecture", "cpu_features"). Matched against a snapshot under the same schema_version: every attribute on the snapshot must be present on the worker with an equal value (except "cpu_features", where the snapshot's hexadecimal bitmask must be a bitwise subset of the worker's); keys only the worker has are ignored, so a worker can gain keys under one schema_version without invalidating older snapshots. last_assigned_generation tracks the last snapshot generation assigned for this Actor during a Suspend or Pause request. Even during Revert, the generation is not decreased to keep track of snapshots that have become stale and need to be cleaned up.

actor.status.snapshots.sandbox_runtime.version.schema_version string

Compatibility schema version (e.g. "v1") defining which runtime and hardware attributes are recorded and how they are computed.

actor.status.snapshots.sandbox_runtime.version.attributes repeated AttributeEntry

Key-value compatibility attributes defined by this schema version, covering both runtime assets (e.g. "sandbox_bundle_hash") and effective guest hardware features after masking (e.g. "architecture", "cpu_features"). Matched against a snapshot under the same schema_version: every attribute on the snapshot must be present on the worker with an equal value (except "cpu_features", where the snapshot's hexadecimal bitmask must be a bitwise subset of the worker's); keys only the worker has are ignored, so a worker can gain keys under one schema_version without invalidating older snapshots. Removing or recomputing a key is a new schema_version, under which older snapshots no longer match. Order as sent does not matter: ate-api-server sorts attributes by key before recording them.

actor.status.snapshots.sandbox_runtime.version.attributes.key string

Attribute name (e.g. "architecture", "cpu_features", "sandbox_bundle_hash").

actor.status.snapshots.sandbox_runtime.version.attributes.value string

Attribute value corresponding to key.

actor.status.last_assigned_generation int32

last_assigned_generation tracks the last snapshot generation assigned for this Actor during a Suspend or Pause request. Even during Revert, the generation is not decreased to keep track of snapshots that have become stale and need to be cleaned up.

actor.status.external_volumes repeated ExternalVolume

Volumes attached to the actor. These volumes only live as long as the actor. They are deleted when the actor is deleted. Each template volume appears at most once.

actor.status.external_volumes.name string

Name of the volume specified in the actor template. Template volume names are DNS labels.

actor.status.external_volumes.storage_volume_id string

The globally unique volume_id returned from the storage system. This will be initially empty during volume creation. Its format is the storage system's own, so it is only bounded and checked for control characters (U+0000-U+0008, U+000B, U+000C, U+000E-U+001F, U+007F-U+009F). The CSI spec caps IDs at 128 bytes but does not require it, so allow some slack. Set once when provisioning completes, then never changed.

actor.status.external_volumes.volume_type string

Internal volume plugin name or CSI driver name, from the StorageClass provisioner. Must be a DNS subdomain, optionally prefixed with "substrate.io/" (per the CSI spec's driver-name syntax).

actor.status.external_volumes.volume_context map<string, string>

volume_context contains metadata returned by the CSI driver during volume provisioning, needed by the node plugin for mounting (e.g. attachment info). Keys and values are the driver's own, so the map is only bounded, not validated.

actor.status.crash ActorCrash

crash records why and when the Actor entered CRASHED. It is set with the CRASHED state and cleared when a revert returns the Actor to SUSPENDED.

actor.status.crash.message string

message is a human-readable description of the failure.

actor.status.crash.crash_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

crash_time is when the Actor entered CRASHED.

actor.status.assigned_node string

assigned_node is the Kubernetes node the Actor is currently attached to (hosting its active worker or its node-local snapshots). Unset when the Actor is detached from any node.

owner identifies the origin and ownership of this snapshot.

actor.status.snapshots.fidelity SnapshotFidelity

fidelity is what this snapshot holds.

actor.status.snapshots.actor_template_uid string

UID of the ActorTemplate whose sandbox this snapshot's guest state was captured from.

actor.status.snapshots.locality string

locality identifies the node holding this snapshot's files (currently the Kubernetes node name). Set when a local pause checkpoint completes, and cleared once the files are deleted from that node; a resume does not delete them.

actor.status.snapshots.durable_snapshot SnapshotStorage

durable_snapshot holds the durable storage representation of this snapshot. Unset when the snapshot only exists locally.

object snapshot is stored in object storage.

DeleteActor

Delete an actor. Only suspended or crashed actors can be deleted unless any_state is set.

Request (DeleteActorRequest)

actor ObjectRef
actor.atespace string

The atespace of the referenced resource. This field should be empty if the target resource is global-scoped, but references to objects in the same atespace as the referrer must still populate this field.

References to atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:required References to non-atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:forbidden

actor.name string

The name of the referenced resource. This field is required.

any_state bool

If true, delete the actor regardless of its state.

options DeleteOptions

Optional per-delete preconditions.

options.version int64

Delete only if the resource is still at this version, that is, unchanged since the caller read it. Zero skips the check.

options.uid string

Delete only if the resource still has this uid, that is, it is the one the caller read and not a later one created under the same name. Empty skips the check.

Response (Actor)

The Actor resource.

References to atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:required References to non-atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:forbidden

actor.name string

The name of the referenced resource. This field is required.

audiences repeated string

The audiences the minted JWT is bound to. Tokens are only issued with audience bindings, so at least one is required.

expiration_seconds int64

Lifetime of the JWT, in seconds.

Response (MintActorJwtResponse)

actor_jwt string

The signed actor JWT. Relying parties verify it with OpenID Connect Discovery against its issuer.

Claims:

  • iss: The issuer URL. Relying parties fetch <iss>/.well-known/openid-configuration to find the signing keys.
  • sub: actor/<atespace>/<name>.
  • aud: The requested audiences, always a JSON array.
  • exp, nbf, iat: Numeric Unix timestamps. nbf is five minutes before iat to allow for clock skew.
  • jti: A random token ID.
  • actor.ate.dev: A JSON object with the actor's atespace, actorName, and actorUID.

The subject and claim name say the token speaks for the actor itself. A token minted for a Substrate component acting on the actor's behalf (WorkerService.MintWorkerActorJwt) uses worker-for-actor in both places instead, so a relying party can grant the two different access.

expire_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

expire_time is when actor_jwt expires. Equal to its exp claim.

MintActorJwtResponse

MintActorCertificate

Create a Substrate-issued SPIFFE certificate asserting the actor identity.

SPIFFE URI: spiffe://${trustdomain}/actor/${atespace}/${actor}

  • Called by the egress gateway when actor client certificate injection is configured for outbound requests.

Request (MintActorCertificateRequest)

actor ObjectRef

The actor for which the certificate should be issued.

Must be a valid actor that currently exists according to the actor store.

actor.atespace string

The atespace of the referenced resource. This field should be empty if the target resource is global-scoped, but references to objects in the same atespace as the referrer must still populate this field.

References to atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:required References to non-atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:forbidden

actor.name string

The name of the referenced resource. This field is required.

actor_uid string

The UID of the actor --- used to guard against deletion and recreation of an actor with the same name.

certificate_signing_request bytes

Request contains DER encoded bytes of a x509 certificate signing request. The signer will ignore the contents of the CSR except to extract the subject public key.

Response (MintActorCertificateResponse)

actor_certificates repeated bytes

Response contains a list of DER encoded certificates. The first entry is the leaf certificate, and any remaining entries are intermediates in leaf-to-root order.

worker references the assigned Worker. This is the field to look the Worker up by; the worker_* fields below are a denormalized copy kept so that readers on a hot path do not have to fetch the Worker at all.

worker_epoch is the Worker's epoch when the Actor was placed on it. 0 if the Worker had not reported one.

actors.status.worker_assignment.sandbox_runtime SandboxRuntime

sandbox_runtime is the sandbox runtime and compatibility version the Actor was started or restored under on this Worker.

actors.status.worker_assignment.sandbox_runtime.sandbox_class string

e.g. "gvisor", "microvm"

actors.status.worker_assignment.sandbox_runtime.version VersionedSandboxCompat

Primary compatibility version stamped onto an actor's snapshot when a checkpoint is taken on this runtime. Snapshots matching version can warm-boot on this runtime. TODO: Add support for additional compatibility versions.

actors.status.worker_assignment.sandbox_runtime.version.schema_version string

Compatibility schema version (e.g. "v1") defining which runtime and hardware attributes are recorded and how they are computed.

actors.status.worker_assignment.sandbox_runtime.version.attributes repeated AttributeEntry

Key-value compatibility attributes defined by this schema version, covering both runtime assets (e.g. "sandbox_bundle_hash") and effective guest hardware features after masking (e.g. "architecture", "cpu_features"). Matched against a snapshot under the same schema_version: every attribute on the snapshot must be present on the worker with an equal value (except "cpu_features", where the snapshot's hexadecimal bitmask must be a bitwise subset of the worker's); keys only the worker has are ignored, so a worker can gain keys under one schema_version without invalidating older snapshots. Removing or recomputing a key is a new schema_version, under which older snapshots no longer match. Order as sent does not matter: ate-api-server sorts attributes by key before recording them.

actors.status.worker_assignment.sandbox_runtime.version.attributes.key string

Attribute name (e.g. "architecture", "cpu_features", "sandbox_bundle_hash").

actors.status.worker_assignment.sandbox_runtime.version.attributes.value string

Attribute value corresponding to key.

actors.status.worker_assignment.worker_spiffe_id string

worker_spiffe_id is the SPIFFE ID worker_pod's certificate carries, copied from Worker.worker_spiffe_id.

actors.status.external_volumes repeated ExternalVolume

Volumes attached to the actor. These volumes only live as long as the actor. They are deleted when the actor is deleted. Each template volume appears at most once.

actors.status.external_volumes.name string

Name of the volume specified in the actor template. Template volume names are DNS labels.

actors.status.external_volumes.storage_volume_id string

The globally unique volume_id returned from the storage system. This will be initially empty during volume creation. Its format is the storage system's own, so it is only bounded and checked for control characters (U+0000-U+0008, U+000B, U+000C, U+000E-U+001F, U+007F-U+009F). The CSI spec caps IDs at 128 bytes but does not require it, so allow some slack. Set once when provisioning completes, then never changed.

actors.status.external_volumes.volume_type string

Internal volume plugin name or CSI driver name, from the StorageClass provisioner. Must be a DNS subdomain, optionally prefixed with "substrate.io/" (per the CSI spec's driver-name syntax).

actors.status.external_volumes.volume_context map<string, string>

volume_context contains metadata returned by the CSI driver during volume provisioning, needed by the node plugin for mounting (e.g. attachment info). Keys and values are the driver's own, so the map is only bounded, not validated.

actors.status.crash ActorCrash

crash records why and when the Actor entered CRASHED. It is set with the CRASHED state and cleared when a revert returns the Actor to SUSPENDED.

actors.status.crash.message string

message is a human-readable description of the failure.

actors.status.crash.crash_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

crash_time is when the Actor entered CRASHED.

actors.status.assigned_node string

assigned_node is the Kubernetes node the Actor is currently attached to (hosting its active worker or its node-local snapshots). Unset when the Actor is detached from any node.

actors.status.snapshots repeated Snapshot

snapshots holds the Actor's active and in-progress snapshot generations.

actors.status.snapshots.uuid string

uuid is the server-generated unique identifier for this snapshot, passed to atelet to identify the local checkpoint on disk and used as the snapshot name in object storage.

actors.status.snapshots.generation int32

generation is the monotonically increasing generation number of this snapshot, starting at 1.

actors.status.snapshots.owner SnapshotOwner

owner identifies the origin and ownership of this snapshot.

actors.status.snapshots.fidelity SnapshotFidelity

fidelity is what this snapshot holds.

actors.status.snapshots.actor_template_uid string

UID of the ActorTemplate whose sandbox this snapshot's guest state was captured from.

actors.status.snapshots.locality string

locality identifies the node holding this snapshot's files (currently the Kubernetes node name). Set when a local pause checkpoint completes, and cleared once the files are deleted from that node; a resume does not delete them.

actors.status.snapshots.durable_snapshot SnapshotStorage

durable_snapshot holds the durable storage representation of this snapshot. Unset when the snapshot only exists locally.

actors.status.snapshots.durable_snapshot.status SnapshotStorageStatus

status is the lifecycle status of the durable snapshot.

actors.status.snapshots.durable_snapshot.object ObjectSnapshot

object snapshot is stored in object storage.

actors.status.snapshots.durable_snapshot.object.snapshot_uri string

snapshot_uri addresses the snapshot's prefix in object storage.

actors.status.snapshots.sandbox_runtime SandboxRuntime

sandbox_runtime is the runtime the actor ran under when the snapshot was taken.

actors.status.snapshots.sandbox_runtime.sandbox_class string

e.g. "gvisor", "microvm"

actors.status.snapshots.sandbox_runtime.version VersionedSandboxCompat

Primary compatibility version stamped onto an actor's snapshot when a checkpoint is taken on this runtime. Snapshots matching version can warm-boot on this runtime. TODO: Add support for additional compatibility versions.

Matched against a snapshot under the same schema_version: every attribute on the snapshot must be present on the worker with an equal value (except "cpu_features", where the snapshot's hexadecimal bitmask must be a bitwise subset of the worker's); keys only the worker has are ignored, so a worker can gain keys under one schema_version without invalidating older snapshots. Removing or recomputing a key is a new schema_version, under which older snapshots no longer match. Order as sent does not matter: ate-api-server sorts attributes by key before recording them.

actors.status.snapshots.sandbox_runtime.version.attributes.key string

Attribute name (e.g. "architecture", "cpu_features", "sandbox_bundle_hash").

Attribute value corresponding to key.

last_assigned_generation tracks the last snapshot generation assigned for this Actor during a Suspend or Pause request. Even during Revert, the generation is not decreased to keep track of snapshots that have become stale and need to be cleaned up.

worker_selector Selector

worker_selector.match_labels map<string, string>

match_labels selects by exact equality on a set of labels.

containers repeated Container
containers.name string
containers.image string

image is the OCI image reference the container runs: [registry/]repository[:tag]@digest. Must be pinned by digest (e.g. "name@sha256:...").

containers.command repeated string

Entrypoint array; when set, the image's ENTRYPOINT and CMD are both ignored and the process argv is command + args. Unlike Kubernetes, $(VAR_NAME) references are NOT expanded.

containers.args repeated string

Arguments to the entrypoint; the image's CMD is used if unset (unless command is set, which discards the image's CMD).

containers.env repeated EnvVar

Env variables to set in the container's process environment. Unlike Kubernetes, $(VAR_NAME) references are NOT expanded in this field.

containers.env.name string

name may be any printable ASCII character except '='.

containers.env.value string

value is the literal value.

containers.wakeup_probe WakeupProbe

wakeup_probe gates each wakeup on this container: ResumeActor returns only after the probe answers HTTP 200. Without it, ResumeActor returns as soon as the container has started, which may be before it listens.

containers.wakeup_probe.http_get HttpGetAction

http_get is the request to poll.

containers.wakeup_probe.http_get.path string

path must be a URL path starting with "/", using only RFC 3986 path-segment characters, without query or fragment. Defaults to "/" when unset.

containers.wakeup_probe.http_get.port int32

port is the container port to connect to.

containers.wakeup_probe.timeout_seconds int32

timeout_seconds is how long to keep polling before giving up. Defaults to 30 when unset.

containers.volume_mounts repeated VolumeMount

Keyed by mount_path: each path hosts exactly one mount, while a volume may be mounted at multiple paths.

containers.volume_mounts.name string

name must match the name of a Volume.

containers.volume_mounts.mount_path string

mount_path within the container. Must be a clean absolute Unix path: must start with '/', not be '/', and contain no ':', '..', '.', '//', trailing '/', or control characters.

containers.security_context SecurityContext

security_context adjusts the container's security settings. Unset leaves the default capability set.

containers.security_context.capabilities Capabilities

capabilities adjusts the Linux capabilities of the container's process.

containers.security_context.capabilities.add repeated string

add lists capabilities to grant on top of the default set. "ALL" is rejected: name the individual capabilities the container needs.

containers.security_context.capabilities.drop repeated string

drop lists capabilities to remove from the default set. "ALL" drops the whole set, so drop+add expresses an exact set rather than a relative one.

containers.resources Resources

resources carries this container's compute limits, enforced inside the actor's sandbox. Only cpu and memory limits are supported.

containers.resources.limits repeated Limits

limits is the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. Only "cpu" and "memory" are supported, each at most once, and each quantity must be greater than zero; the cpu limit must be less than 1000 cores.

containers.resources.limits.name string
containers.resources.limits.quantity string

quantity is in Kubernetes resource.Quantity string form (e.g. "500m", "2Gi").

volumes repeated Volume
volumes.name string

name of the volume. Must be a DNS label.

volumes.durable_dir DurableDirVolumeSource

Exactly one of durable_dir / external_volume_template / image / system_info must be set.

volumes.external_volume_template ExternalVolumeTemplate
volumes.external_volume_template.capacity string

capacity of the volume to create, in Kubernetes resource.Quantity string form (e.g. "10Gi"). Required.

volumes.external_volume_template.storage_class_name string

storage_class_name names the cluster-scoped Kubernetes StorageClass to create the volume from. Required.

volumes.system_info SystemInfoVolumeSource
volumes.system_info.data_sources repeated SystemInfoDataSource

data_sources lists the projections to place within the volume. At most one actor_metadata entry may appear, and file paths must be unique across all entries.

volumes.system_info.data_sources.actor_metadata ActorMetadataDataSource

Exactly one of actor_metadata / trust_bundle must be set.

volumes.system_info.data_sources.actor_metadata.items repeated ActorMetadataItem

items must not project the same field twice, and item paths must be unique.

volumes.system_info.data_sources.actor_metadata.items.field ActorMetadataField
volumes.system_info.data_sources.actor_metadata.items.path string

path must be a clean relative Unix path: at most 16 '/'-separated segments, none of them empty, '.' or '..', and no NUL byte.

volumes.system_info.data_sources.trust_bundle TrustBundleDataSource
volumes.system_info.data_sources.trust_bundle.names repeated string

One or more named trust bundles to unify and place at the specified path.

Substrate supports a short list of predefined names:

  • egress-mitm.ate.dev --- The trust anchors for the Substrate egress gateway TLS man-in-the-middle interceptor.

  • system-roots.ate.dev --- A selection of well-known public CA root certificates, built into Substrate

volumes.system_info.data_sources.trust_bundle.path string

path must be a clean relative Unix path: at most 16 '/'-separated segments, none of them empty, '.' or '..', and no NUL byte.

volumes.image ImageVolumeSource

image mounts the contents of an OCI image, read-only.

volumes.image.reference string

reference is the OCI image reference. Must include a digest (e.g. "name@sha256:...").

snapshot_config SnapshotConfig
snapshot_config.storage_location string

storage_location is the base object-storage URI snapshots of actors on this version are stored under. Required.

snapshot_config.preferred_fidelity SnapshotFidelity

preferred_fidelity is the highest fidelity the system packages when it snapshots the actor, on pause (node-local) and on suspend (uploaded). It is a best-effort ceiling, not a guarantee: the system never packages more than this level, and it may package less when a layer cannot be captured or is too expensive to capture at the time, for example memory under host pressure. A process resumed in place on its worker keeps its memory regardless of this setting. ROOTFS requires sandbox_config.sandbox_class "microvm". Defaults to MEMORY when unset.

snapshot_config.golden_snapshot_config GoldenSnapshotConfig

golden_snapshot_config configures automated golden snapshot creation. Golden snapshots are enabled when this config is omitted.

snapshot_config.golden_snapshot_config.mode GoldenSnapshotMode

mode defaults to ENABLED when unspecified. DISABLED skips creating the template's golden actor and tag.

sandbox_config SandboxConfig

sandbox_config selects the sandbox runtime this version's actors run on.

sandbox_config.sandbox_class string

sandbox_class selects the sandbox runtime family: "gvisor" or "microvm". Snapshots are not portable across classes.

sandbox_config.config_name string

config_name names the cluster-scoped SandboxConfig Kubernetes object supplying the sandbox binaries. Required; must match sandbox_class.

resources Resources

resources is the actor's compute size. Both cpu and memory limits are required: the scheduler books them against worker capacity, and a micro-VM is booted at that size.

resources.limits repeated Limits

limits is the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. Only "cpu" and "memory" are supported, each at most once, and each quantity must be greater than zero; the cpu limit must be less than 1000 cores.

resources.limits.name string
resources.limits.quantity string

quantity is in Kubernetes resource.Quantity string form (e.g. "500m", "2Gi").

status ActorTemplateStatus
status.golden_snapshot_status GoldenSnapshotStatus
status.golden_snapshot_status.golden_tag ObjectRef

golden_tag owns the immutable snapshot built by the template controller. Set after tagging the snapshot and deleting the temporary golden Actor.

status.golden_snapshot_status.golden_tag.atespace string

The atespace of the referenced resource. This field should be empty if the target resource is global-scoped, but references to objects in the same atespace as the referrer must still populate this field.

References to atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:required References to non-atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:forbidden

status.golden_snapshot_status.golden_tag.name string

The name of the referenced resource. This field is required.

status.golden_snapshot_status.snapshot_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

snapshot_time is when the golden-actor warmup ends and the golden snapshot may be taken.

status.golden_snapshot_status.error_message string

error_message is set when the golden snapshot build fails and will not be retried, formatted as <Reason>: <detail>. A nonempty value is terminal.

metadata.update_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

update_time is the time the resource was last updated.

This field is ignored on input.

rules repeated EgressRule

Rules are an unordered set of allows. Traffic is denied when no rule matches.

For a given destination name and port, exactly one rule decides, whatever its protocol. When more than one rule matches, the winner is chosen by these criteria, in order, moving to the next one on a tie:

  • A matching hostname without a wildcard.
  • A matching port number rather than all ports.

Two rules with the same pattern on the same port, or both on all ports, are rejected at admission.

These criteria apply within a protocol and across protocols that decide on the same input, such as an https and a tls_passthrough rule that match the same pattern. Only the winning rule's effects are applied.

rules.http HttpRule

Cleartext HTTP to the named hosts: HTTP/1.1, and h2c as used by gRPC. TLS to these names is not allowed by this rule.

rules.http.hostnames repeated string

Hostname patterns: a DNS name, or a DNS name with "*" as its leftmost label. The rule matches when any pattern matches.

The DNS name must conform to RFC 1034 and RFC 1123. It must be lowercase and must not have a trailing dot.

A wildcard replaces the complete leftmost label. ".example.com" matches exactly one non-empty label, such as "api.example.com". It does not match "example.com" or "nested.api.example.com". "" alone matches every name. No other wildcard syntax is accepted. A pattern without a wildcard matches only the complete normalized name. Patterns may overlap: the rule ranks by the most specific pattern that matches the destination.

Internationalized names must use their IDNA A-label (punycode) form; no Unicode conversion is performed. URLs, IP addresses, names with ports, malformed DNS names (for example, "foo..example.com"), and more than one trailing dot are invalid.

rules.http.ports Ports

Ports of the destination the Actor connected to. A port in a request's authority is neither matched nor dialed. Defaults to port 80.

rules.http.ports.all AllPorts

Every port.

rules.http.ports.numbers repeated int32

Port numbers, without repeats.

rules.http.effects HttpRuleEffects

Effects do not authorize traffic. They are applied only when this is the deciding rule.

rules.http.effects.replace_headers repeated CredentialHeader

Replaces placeholder request headers with credentials. A header is replaced only when the request from the Actor carries it; requests without the header are forwarded unchanged, so a credential reaches only the requests that ask for it. Header names must be unique case-insensitively.

Replacement is supported on HTTP and HTTPS. On HTTP, the gateway does not originate TLS to the destination. Without separate transport protection, observers can read the credential and attackers on the path can modify the request. Deployments may encrypt traffic outside the gateway; policy authors must account for any unprotected segments between credential injection and the intended destination.

rules.http.effects.replace_headers.header string

The case-insensitive HTTP request header to replace when present.

rules.http.effects.replace_headers.prefix string

Prepended verbatim to the credential value. Include any desired separator; for example, use "Bearer " (including the space) for Authorization.

rules.http.effects.replace_headers.credential_uri string

Source-agnostic reference interpreted by a registered credential provider: ate-secret://<provider-class>/<provider-name>/<provider-specific-tail>

Exactly one of credential_uri and actor_jwt must be set.

rules.http.effects.replace_headers.actor_jwt ActorJwtSource

A Substrate-issued JWT asserting the identity of the Actor that sent the request.

rules.http.effects.replace_headers.actor_jwt.audiences repeated string

The audiences the JWT is bound to, which become its aud claim.

rules.http.effects.replace_headers.actor_jwt.expiration_seconds int64

Lifetime of each JWT, in seconds.

rules.https HttpsRule

HTTPS to the named hosts, intercepted (man-in-the-middle) so the gateway can authorize and modify each request. HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 inside the TLS connection; HTTP/3 is not supported.

rules.https.hostnames repeated string

Server names matched against the SNI, in the pattern syntax of HttpRule.hostnames.

rules.https.ports Ports

Ports of the destination the Actor connected to. Defaults to port 443.

rules.https.ports.all AllPorts

Every port.

rules.https.ports.numbers repeated int32

Port numbers, without repeats.

rules.https.effects HttpRuleEffects

Effects do not authorize traffic. They are applied only when this is the deciding rule.

rules.https.effects.replace_headers repeated CredentialHeader

Replaces placeholder request headers with credentials. A header is replaced only when the request from the Actor carries it; requests without the header are forwarded unchanged, so a credential reaches only the requests that ask for it. Header names must be unique case-insensitively.

Replacement is supported on HTTP and HTTPS. On HTTP, the gateway does not originate TLS to the destination. Without separate transport protection, observers can read the credential and attackers on the path can modify the request. Deployments may encrypt traffic outside the gateway; policy authors must account for any unprotected segments between credential injection and the intended destination.

rules.https.effects.replace_headers.header string

The case-insensitive HTTP request header to replace when present.

rules.https.effects.replace_headers.prefix string

Prepended verbatim to the credential value. Include any desired separator; for example, use "Bearer " (including the space) for Authorization.

rules.https.effects.replace_headers.credential_uri string

Source-agnostic reference interpreted by a registered credential provider: ate-secret://<provider-class>/<provider-name>/<provider-specific-tail>

Exactly one of credential_uri and actor_jwt must be set.

rules.https.effects.replace_headers.actor_jwt ActorJwtSource

A Substrate-issued JWT asserting the identity of the Actor that sent the request.

rules.https.effects.replace_headers.actor_jwt.audiences repeated string

The audiences the JWT is bound to, which become its aud claim.

rules.https.effects.replace_headers.actor_jwt.expiration_seconds int64

Lifetime of each JWT, in seconds.

rules.tls_passthrough TlsPassthroughRule

TLS to the named servers, forwarded without decryption.

rules.tls_passthrough.hostnames repeated string

Server names matched against the SNI, in the pattern syntax of HttpRule.hostnames.

rules.tls_passthrough.ports Ports

Ports of the destination the Actor connected to.

rules.tls_passthrough.ports.all AllPorts

Every port.

rules.tls_passthrough.ports.numbers repeated int32

Port numbers, without repeats.

{  "metadata": {    "atespace": "prod",    "name": "default",    "uid": "1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a3b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d",    "version": "2",    "createTime": "2026-08-01T18:22:04Z",    "updateTime": "2026-08-02T11:05:40Z"  },  "rules": [    {      "https": {        "hostnames": [          "api.example.com"        ],        "effects": {          "replaceHeaders": [            {              "header": "Authorization",              "prefix": "Bearer ",              "credentialUri": "ate-secret://gcp-secret-manager/prod/checkout-api-key"            }          ]        }      }    },    {      "tlsPassthrough": {        "hostnames": [          "*.googleapis.com"        ],        "ports": {          "numbers": [            443          ]        }      }    }  ]}

egress_policy.rules repeated EgressRule

Rules are an unordered set of allows. Traffic is denied when no rule matches.

For a given destination name and port, exactly one rule decides, whatever its protocol. When more than one rule matches, the winner is chosen by these criteria, in order, moving to the next one on a tie:

  • A matching hostname without a wildcard.
  • A matching port number rather than all ports.

Two rules with the same pattern on the same port, or both on all ports, are rejected at admission.

These criteria apply within a protocol and across protocols that decide on the same input, such as an https and a tls_passthrough rule that match the same pattern. Only the winning rule's effects are applied.

egress_policy.rules.http HttpRule

Cleartext HTTP to the named hosts: HTTP/1.1, and h2c as used by gRPC. TLS to these names is not allowed by this rule.

egress_policy.rules.http.hostnames repeated string

Hostname patterns: a DNS name, or a DNS name with "*" as its leftmost label. The rule matches when any pattern matches.

The DNS name must conform to RFC 1034 and RFC 1123. It must be lowercase and must not have a trailing dot.

A wildcard replaces the complete leftmost label. ".example.com" matches exactly one non-empty label, such as "api.example.com". It does not match "example.com" or "nested.api.example.com". "" alone matches every name. No other wildcard syntax is accepted. A pattern without a wildcard matches only the complete normalized name. Patterns may overlap: the rule ranks by the most specific pattern that matches the destination.

Internationalized names must use their IDNA A-label (punycode) form; no Unicode conversion is performed. URLs, IP addresses, names with ports, malformed DNS names (for example, "foo..example.com"), and more than one trailing dot are invalid.

egress_policy.rules.http.ports Ports

Ports of the destination the Actor connected to. A port in a request's authority is neither matched nor dialed. Defaults to port 80.

egress_policy.rules.http.ports.all AllPorts

Every port.

egress_policy.rules.http.ports.numbers repeated int32

Port numbers, without repeats.

egress_policy.rules.http.effects HttpRuleEffects

Effects do not authorize traffic. They are applied only when this is the deciding rule.

egress_policy.rules.http.effects.replace_headers repeated CredentialHeader

Replaces placeholder request headers with credentials. A header is replaced only when the request from the Actor carries it; requests without the header are forwarded unchanged, so a credential reaches only the requests that ask for it. Header names must be unique case-insensitively.

Replacement is supported on HTTP and HTTPS. On HTTP, the gateway does not originate TLS to the destination. Without separate transport protection, observers can read the credential and attackers on the path can modify the request. Deployments may encrypt traffic outside the gateway; policy authors must account for any unprotected segments between credential injection and the intended destination.

egress_policy.rules.http.effects.replace_headers.header string

The case-insensitive HTTP request header to replace when present.

egress_policy.rules.http.effects.replace_headers.prefix string

Prepended verbatim to the credential value. Include any desired separator; for example, use "Bearer " (including the space) for Authorization.

egress_policy.rules.http.effects.replace_headers.credential_uri string

Source-agnostic reference interpreted by a registered credential provider: ate-secret://<provider-class>/<provider-name>/<provider-specific-tail>

Exactly one of credential_uri and actor_jwt must be set.

egress_policy.rules.http.effects.replace_headers.actor_jwt ActorJwtSource

A Substrate-issued JWT asserting the identity of the Actor that sent the request.

egress_policy.rules.http.effects.replace_headers.actor_jwt.audiences repeated string

The audiences the JWT is bound to, which become its aud claim.

egress_policy.rules.http.effects.replace_headers.actor_jwt.expiration_seconds int64

Lifetime of each JWT, in seconds.

egress_policy.rules.https HttpsRule

HTTPS to the named hosts, intercepted (man-in-the-middle) so the gateway can authorize and modify each request. HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 inside the TLS connection; HTTP/3 is not supported.

egress_policy.rules.https.hostnames repeated string

Server names matched against the SNI, in the pattern syntax of HttpRule.hostnames.

egress_policy.rules.https.ports Ports

Ports of the destination the Actor connected to. Defaults to port 443.

egress_policy.rules.https.ports.all AllPorts

Every port.

egress_policy.rules.https.ports.numbers repeated int32

Port numbers, without repeats.

Replaces placeholder request headers with credentials. A header is replaced only when the request from the Actor carries it; requests without the header are forwarded unchanged, so a credential reaches only the requests that ask for it. Header names must be unique case-insensitively.

Tag

atespace

Tag is an Atespace-owned, stable name for one external snapshot. The external snapshot pointed by a tag is a copy of an actor snapshot. The snapshot is copied when the tag is created, and deleted when the tag is. Its owning Atespace cannot be deleted until the tag is removed.

Methods

MethodDescriptionRequestResponse
CreateTag

Tag the external snapshot a suspended Actor holds. The tag gets its own copy of that snapshot, so suspending or deleting the Actor afterwards cannot collect it.

 CreateTagRequest Tag
GetTag

Get a Tag.

 GetTagRequest Tag
ListTags

List Tags.

 ListTagsRequest ListTagsResponse
UpdateTag

Publish or unpublish a Tag without changing its address.

 UpdateTagRequest Tag
DeleteTag

Delete a Tag and the external snapshot it owns. Actors created from the tag that have not yet been suspended still point at that external snapshot and become unrecoverable, so do not delete a tag while such Actors exist.

 DeleteTagRequest Tag

status TagStatus

status is set by the control plane; it is ignored on write.

status.snapshot Snapshot

snapshot is the external snapshot this tag points at: the tag's own copy, stored under a prefix keyed on the tag's UID. It is recorded with its durable_snapshot PENDING right after the tag is reserved, before anything is copied, and transitions to COMPLETED once the copy finishes: a tag never moves between snapshots and is usable only once COMPLETED. Unset until it is recorded; a tag whose creation failed first never gets one.

status.snapshot.uuid string

uuid is the server-generated unique identifier for this snapshot, passed to atelet to identify the local checkpoint on disk and used as the snapshot name in object storage.

status.snapshot.generation int32

generation is the monotonically increasing generation number of this snapshot, starting at 1.

status.snapshot.owner SnapshotOwner

owner identifies the origin and ownership of this snapshot.

status.snapshot.fidelity SnapshotFidelity

fidelity is what this snapshot holds.

status.snapshot.actor_template_uid string

UID of the ActorTemplate whose sandbox this snapshot's guest state was captured from.

status.snapshot.locality string

locality identifies the node holding this snapshot's files (currently the Kubernetes node name). Set when a local pause checkpoint completes, and cleared once the files are deleted from that node; a resume does not delete them.

status.snapshot.durable_snapshot SnapshotStorage

durable_snapshot holds the durable storage representation of this snapshot. Unset when the snapshot only exists locally.

status.snapshot.durable_snapshot.status SnapshotStorageStatus

status is the lifecycle status of the durable snapshot.

status.snapshot.durable_snapshot.object ObjectSnapshot

object snapshot is stored in object storage.

status.snapshot.durable_snapshot.object.snapshot_uri string

snapshot_uri addresses the snapshot's prefix in object storage.

status.snapshot.sandbox_runtime SandboxRuntime

sandbox_runtime is the runtime the actor ran under when the snapshot was taken.

status.snapshot.sandbox_runtime.sandbox_class string

e.g. "gvisor", "microvm"

status.snapshot.sandbox_runtime.version VersionedSandboxCompat

Primary compatibility version stamped onto an actor's snapshot when a checkpoint is taken on this runtime. Snapshots matching version can warm-boot on this runtime. TODO: Add support for additional compatibility versions.

status.snapshot.sandbox_runtime.version.schema_version string

Compatibility schema version (e.g. "v1") defining which runtime and hardware attributes are recorded and how they are computed.

status.snapshot.sandbox_runtime.version.attributes repeated AttributeEntry

Key-value compatibility attributes defined by this schema version, covering both runtime assets (e.g. "sandbox_bundle_hash") and effective guest hardware features after masking (e.g. "architecture", "cpu_features"). Matched against a snapshot under the same schema_version: every attribute on the snapshot must be present on the worker with an equal value (except "cpu_features", where the snapshot's hexadecimal bitmask must be a bitwise subset of the worker's); keys only the worker has are ignored, so a worker can gain keys under one schema_version without invalidating older snapshots. Removing or recomputing a key is a new schema_version, under which older snapshots no longer match. Order as sent does not matter: ate-api-server sorts attributes by key before recording them.

status.snapshot.sandbox_runtime.version.attributes.key string

Attribute name (e.g. "architecture", "cpu_features", "sandbox_bundle_hash").

status.snapshot.sandbox_runtime.version.attributes.value string

Attribute value corresponding to key.

status.actor_template_uid string

UID of the ActorTemplate the snapshot was taken under. Actors can only be seeded from a tag under the same template.

scope TagScope

scope controls who may create an Actor from this tag.

source_actor ObjectRef

source_actor is the suspended Actor whose external snapshot this tag captures. The tag lives in this Actor's Atespace. Set once at creation and immutable afterward.

source_actor.atespace string

The atespace of the referenced resource. This field should be empty if the target resource is global-scoped, but references to objects in the same atespace as the referrer must still populate this field.

References to atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:required References to non-atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:forbidden

source_actor.name string

The name of the referenced resource. This field is required.

tags.status.snapshot.sandbox_runtime.version VersionedSandboxCompat

Primary compatibility version stamped onto an actor's snapshot when a checkpoint is taken on this runtime. Snapshots matching version can warm-boot on this runtime. TODO: Add support for additional compatibility versions.

tags.status.snapshot.sandbox_runtime.version.schema_version string

Compatibility schema version (e.g. "v1") defining which runtime and hardware attributes are recorded and how they are computed.

tags.status.snapshot.sandbox_runtime.version.attributes repeated AttributeEntry

Key-value compatibility attributes defined by this schema version, covering both runtime assets (e.g. "sandbox_bundle_hash") and effective guest hardware features after masking (e.g. "architecture", "cpu_features"). Matched against a snapshot under the same schema_version: every attribute on the snapshot must be present on the worker with an equal value (except "cpu_features", where the snapshot's hexadecimal bitmask must be a bitwise subset of the worker's); keys only the worker has are ignored, so a worker can gain keys under one schema_version without invalidating older snapshots. Removing or recomputing a key is a new schema_version, under which older snapshots no longer match. Order as sent does not matter: ate-api-server sorts attributes by key before recording them.

Attribute name (e.g. "architecture", "cpu_features", "sandbox_bundle_hash").

tags.status.snapshot.sandbox_runtime.version.attributes.value string

Attribute value corresponding to key.

tag.status.snapshot Snapshot

snapshot is the external snapshot this tag points at: the tag's own copy, stored under a prefix keyed on the tag's UID. It is recorded with its durable_snapshot PENDING right after the tag is reserved, before anything is copied, and transitions to COMPLETED once the copy finishes: a tag never moves between snapshots and is usable only once COMPLETED. Unset until it is recorded; a tag whose creation failed first never gets one.

tag.status.snapshot.locality string

locality identifies the node holding this snapshot's files (currently the Kubernetes node name). Set when a local pause checkpoint completes, and cleared once the files are deleted from that node; a resume does not delete them.

durable_snapshot holds the durable storage representation of this snapshot. Unset when the snapshot only exists locally.

DeleteTag

Delete a Tag and the external snapshot it owns. Actors created from the tag that have not yet been suspended still point at that external snapshot and become unrecoverable, so do not delete a tag while such Actors exist.

Request (DeleteTagRequest)

tag ObjectRef
tag.atespace string

The atespace of the referenced resource. This field should be empty if the target resource is global-scoped, but references to objects in the same atespace as the referrer must still populate this field.

References to atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:required References to non-atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:forbidden

tag.name string

The name of the referenced resource. This field is required.

options DeleteOptions

Optional per-delete preconditions.

options.version int64

Delete only if the resource is still at this version, that is, unchanged since the caller read it. Zero skips the check.

options.uid string

Delete only if the resource still has this uid, that is, it is the one the caller read and not a later one created under the same name. Empty skips the check.

Response (Tag)

Worker

global

Worker is a schedulable worker pod.

Global-scoped: metadata.atespace is always empty. metadata.name is assigned by the control plane and is opaque to clients — never parse it or derive it from anything else; read pod identity from the named fields below.

labels and epoch are the only mutable fields; every other field is either immutable after creation or output-only. UpdateWorker replaces the whole resource, so an immutable field that a request changes — including by omitting it, which would clear it — is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

Subresources

  • ActorAssignment

Methods

MethodDescriptionRequestResponse
ListWorkers

List Workers.

 ListWorkersRequest ListWorkersResponse
GetWorker

Get a Worker.

 GetWorkerRequest Worker
CreateWorker

Register a Worker. Called once its Pod has an IP. A Worker is registered UNAVAILABLE and takes no Actors until MarkWorkerAvailable.

 CreateWorkerRequest Worker
UpdateWorker

Update observed pool state on a Worker.

 UpdateWorkerRequest Worker
DeleteWorker

Deregister a Worker. Does not cascade: the caller is responsible for cleaning up related resources first.

 DeleteWorkerRequest Worker
DrainWorker

Mark a Worker as terminating so the scheduler stops routing new Actors to it. Idempotent; one-way. Deliberately leaves any bound Actor alone. Returns ABORTED if another write lands on the Worker first; retry.

 DrainWorkerRequest DrainWorkerResponse
MarkWorkerAvailable

Mark an UNAVAILABLE Worker ACTIVE so the scheduler places Actors on it. Idempotent. Returns FAILED_PRECONDITION for a DRAINING Worker, and ABORTED if another write lands on the Worker first; retry.

 MarkWorkerAvailableRequest MarkWorkerAvailableResponse
MarkWorkerUnavailable

Mark an ACTIVE Worker UNAVAILABLE so the scheduler stops placing Actors on it, as while its Pod is not Ready. Idempotent. Leaves any bound Actor alone. Returns FAILED_PRECONDITION for a DRAINING Worker, and ABORTED if another write lands on the Worker first; retry.

 MarkWorkerUnavailableRequest MarkWorkerUnavailableResponse

Fields

metadata ResourceMetadata

Output-only: name, uid, version and timestamps are all server-assigned. uid and version are echoed back on UpdateWorker as preconditions.

metadata.atespace string

atespace is the namespace the resource belongs to. Empty for global-scoped resources. Caller-specified at creation and immutable thereafter.

Atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:required Non-atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:forbidden

metadata.name string

name is the resource's name, unique within its atespace (or globally, for global-scoped resources). Caller-specified at creation and immutable thereafter.

metadata.uid string

uid is a server-assigned, globally unique identifier for this resource. Immutable throughout the lifecycle of the resource.

This field is ignored during create operations and used as precondition for update operations.

metadata.version int64

version is increased on every mutation.

This field is ignored during create operations and used as precondition for update operations.

metadata.create_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

create_time is the time the resource was created.

This field is ignored on input.

metadata.update_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

update_time is the time the resource was last updated.

This field is ignored on input.

worker_namespace string

Kubernetes coordinates. Immutable, set at creation.

worker_pool string
worker_pod string
worker_pod_uid string
node_name string
ips repeated string

ips are the worker pod's IPs, at most one per IP family, in the order Kubernetes reports them; the first is in the cluster's primary family.

worker_spiffe_id string

worker_spiffe_id is the SPIFFE ID the worker pod's certificate carries. atenet-router requires it on the certificate of the worker's atunnel.

sandbox_class string

sandbox_class mirrors the WorkerPool's default sandbox class

labels map<string, string>

labels mirror the WorkerPool object's Kubernetes labels, which selectors match against. Kubernetes does not cap an object's label count, so the bound below is a generous guardrail, not a mirror of an upstream limit.

epoch int64

epoch counts the runs of the worker pod's worker container: 1 for its first run and one more for each restart. 0 means it has not been reported.

A restarted worker has lost the sandboxes of the Actors it was hosting, so once epoch rises the control plane crashes every Actor placed during an earlier epoch; status.observed_epoch reports when that is done. It may only increase.

status WorkerStatus

Output-only server-managed state. Absent from Create/Update request payloads; whatever a request carries here is ignored. A client moves state only through DrainWorker, MarkWorkerAvailable and MarkWorkerUnavailable, and the assignments are the scheduler's.

status.state WorkerState
status.capacity WorkerResources

The total resource capacity of the Worker.

A Worker should report every dimension of resources it has available to be consumed by Actors. Any resource not specified here is assumed to be 0. An Actor which requests a resource which is not present in a Worker's capacity will prevent that Actor from running on that Worker.

Shrinking capacity below allocated prevents new placements but does not evicts running Actors.

status.capacity.resources Resources

Resources match the Actor's definition of resources. They are matched by name and used for placement.

status.capacity.resources.limits repeated Limits

limits is the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. Only "cpu" and "memory" are supported, each at most once, and each quantity must be greater than zero; the cpu limit must be less than 1000 cores.

status.capacity.resources.limits.name string
status.capacity.resources.limits.quantity string

quantity is in Kubernetes resource.Quantity string form (e.g. "500m", "2Gi").

status.capacity.actors int32

A count of Actors. Workers can use this to limit the number of Actors that can be placed on them, constraining the costs of other things that are not captured in the resources above, but which still have costs - netns, mounts, file descriptors, etc.

status.allocated WorkerResources

The allocated resources of the Worker. This is the sum of all the resources consumed by the Actors currently assigned to this Worker.

status.allocated.resources Resources

Resources match the Actor's definition of resources. They are matched by name and used for placement.

status.allocated.resources.limits repeated Limits

limits is the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. Only "cpu" and "memory" are supported, each at most once, and each quantity must be greater than zero; the cpu limit must be less than 1000 cores.

status.allocated.resources.limits.name string
status.allocated.resources.limits.quantity string

quantity is in Kubernetes resource.Quantity string form (e.g. "500m", "2Gi").

status.allocated.actors int32

A count of Actors. Workers can use this to limit the number of Actors that can be placed on them, constraining the costs of other things that are not captured in the resources above, but which still have costs - netns, mounts, file descriptors, etc.

status.observed_epoch int64

observed_epoch is the latest epoch whose earlier Actors the control plane has crashed and released. While it is below epoch, Actors placed before the worker's last restart may still be reported as running.

workers.status.restorable_runtimes.version.schema_version string

Compatibility schema version (e.g. "v1") defining which runtime and hardware attributes are recorded and how they are computed.

workers.status.restorable_runtimes.version.attributes repeated AttributeEntry

Key-value compatibility attributes defined by this schema version, covering both runtime assets (e.g. "sandbox_bundle_hash") and effective guest hardware features after masking (e.g. "architecture", "cpu_features"). Matched against a snapshot under the same schema_version: every attribute on the snapshot must be present on the worker with an equal value (except "cpu_features", where the snapshot's hexadecimal bitmask must be a bitwise subset of the worker's); keys only the worker has are ignored, so a worker can gain keys under one schema_version without invalidating older snapshots. Removing or recomputing a key is a new schema_version, under which older snapshots no longer match. Order as sent does not matter: ate-api-server sorts attributes by key before recording them.

workers.status.restorable_runtimes.version.attributes.key string

Attribute name (e.g. "architecture", "cpu_features", "sandbox_bundle_hash").

workers.status.restorable_runtimes.version.attributes.value string

Attribute value corresponding to key.

next_page_token string

Pagination token for the next page. Empty if this is the last page.

CreateWorker

Register a Worker. Called once its Pod has an IP. A Worker is registered UNAVAILABLE and takes no Actors until MarkWorkerAvailable.

Request (CreateWorkerRequest)

worker Worker

The Worker to register.

worker.metadata ResourceMetadata

Output-only: name, uid, version and timestamps are all server-assigned. uid and version are echoed back on UpdateWorker as preconditions.

worker.metadata.atespace string

atespace is the namespace the resource belongs to. Empty for global-scoped resources. Caller-specified at creation and immutable thereafter.

Atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:required Non-atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:forbidden

worker.metadata.name string

name is the resource's name, unique within its atespace (or globally, for global-scoped resources). Caller-specified at creation and immutable thereafter.

worker.metadata.uid string

uid is a server-assigned, globally unique identifier for this resource. Immutable throughout the lifecycle of the resource.

This field is ignored during create operations and used as precondition for update operations.

worker.metadata.version int64

version is increased on every mutation.

This field is ignored during create operations and used as precondition for update operations.

worker.metadata.create_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

create_time is the time the resource was created.

This field is ignored on input.

worker.metadata.update_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

update_time is the time the resource was last updated.

This field is ignored on input.

worker.worker_namespace string

Kubernetes coordinates. Immutable, set at creation.

worker.worker_pool string
worker.worker_pod string
worker.worker_pod_uid string
worker.node_name string
worker.ips repeated string

ips are the worker pod's IPs, at most one per IP family, in the order Kubernetes reports them; the first is in the cluster's primary family.

worker.worker_spiffe_id string

worker_spiffe_id is the SPIFFE ID the worker pod's certificate carries. atenet-router requires it on the certificate of the worker's atunnel.

worker.sandbox_class string

sandbox_class mirrors the WorkerPool's default sandbox class

worker.labels map<string, string>

labels mirror the WorkerPool object's Kubernetes labels, which selectors match against. Kubernetes does not cap an object's label count, so the bound below is a generous guardrail, not a mirror of an upstream limit.

worker.epoch int64

epoch counts the runs of the worker pod's worker container: 1 for its first run and one more for each restart. 0 means it has not been reported.

A restarted worker has lost the sandboxes of the Actors it was hosting, so once epoch rises the control plane crashes every Actor placed during an earlier epoch; status.observed_epoch reports when that is done. It may only increase.

worker.status WorkerStatus

Output-only server-managed state. Absent from Create/Update request payloads; whatever a request carries here is ignored. A client moves state only through DrainWorker, MarkWorkerAvailable and MarkWorkerUnavailable, and the assignments are the scheduler's.

worker.status.state WorkerState
worker.status.capacity WorkerResources

The total resource capacity of the Worker.

A Worker should report every dimension of resources it has available to be consumed by Actors. Any resource not specified here is assumed to be 0. An Actor which requests a resource which is not present in a Worker's capacity will prevent that Actor from running on that Worker.

Shrinking capacity below allocated prevents new placements but does not evicts running Actors.

worker.status.capacity.resources Resources

Resources match the Actor's definition of resources. They are matched by name and used for placement.

worker.status.capacity.resources.limits repeated Limits

limits is the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. Only "cpu" and "memory" are supported, each at most once, and each quantity must be greater than zero; the cpu limit must be less than 1000 cores.

worker.status.capacity.resources.limits.name string
worker.status.capacity.resources.limits.quantity string

quantity is in Kubernetes resource.Quantity string form (e.g. "500m", "2Gi").

worker.status.capacity.actors int32

A count of Actors. Workers can use this to limit the number of Actors that can be placed on them, constraining the costs of other things that are not captured in the resources above, but which still have costs - netns, mounts, file descriptors, etc.

worker.status.allocated WorkerResources

The allocated resources of the Worker. This is the sum of all the resources consumed by the Actors currently assigned to this Worker.

worker.status.allocated.resources Resources

Resources match the Actor's definition of resources. They are matched by name and used for placement.

worker.status.allocated.resources.limits repeated Limits

limits is the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. Only "cpu" and "memory" are supported, each at most once, and each quantity must be greater than zero; the cpu limit must be less than 1000 cores.

worker.status.allocated.resources.limits.name string
worker.status.allocated.resources.limits.quantity string

quantity is in Kubernetes resource.Quantity string form (e.g. "500m", "2Gi").

worker.status.allocated.actors int32

A count of Actors. Workers can use this to limit the number of Actors that can be placed on them, constraining the costs of other things that are not captured in the resources above, but which still have costs - netns, mounts, file descriptors, etc.

worker.status.observed_epoch int64

observed_epoch is the latest epoch whose earlier Actors the control plane has crashed and released. While it is below epoch, Actors placed before the worker's last restart may still be reported as running.

UpdateWorker

Update observed pool state on a Worker.

Request (UpdateWorkerRequest)

worker Worker

The Worker to update. worker.metadata.name identifies which resource to update. atespace is always empty; Workers are global-scoped. worker.metadata.version and worker.metadata.uid are required preconditions.

labels is the only field an update may change. Every other field is replaced with what the request carries, and a field left unset is cleared — so read the Worker, change what you mean to change, and send the whole thing back. A request that alters an immutable field, by changing it or by omitting it, returns INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the field. status is output-only and whatever it carries is ignored.

DeleteWorker

Deregister a Worker. Does not cascade: the caller is responsible for cleaning up related resources first.

Request (DeleteWorkerRequest)

worker ObjectRef

The Worker to deregister.

worker.atespace string

The atespace of the referenced resource. This field should be empty if the target resource is global-scoped, but references to objects in the same atespace as the referrer must still populate this field.

References to atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:required References to non-atespaced resources should add +k8s:subfield(atespace)=+k8s:forbidden

worker.name string

The name of the referenced resource. This field is required.

options DeleteOptions

Optional per-delete preconditions.

options.version int64

Delete only if the resource is still at this version, that is, unchanged since the caller read it. Zero skips the check.

options.uid string

Delete only if the resource still has this uid, that is, it is the one the caller read and not a later one created under the same name. Empty skips the check.

The Worker resource.

DrainWorker

Mark a Worker as terminating so the scheduler stops routing new Actors to it. Idempotent; one-way. Deliberately leaves any bound Actor alone. Returns ABORTED if another write lands on the Worker first; retry.

Matched against a snapshot under the same schema_version: every attribute on the snapshot must be present on the worker with an equal value (except "cpu_features", where the snapshot's hexadecimal bitmask must be a bitwise subset of the worker's); keys only the worker has are ignored, so a worker can gain keys under one schema_version without invalidating older snapshots. Removing or recomputing a key is a new schema_version, under which older snapshots no longer match. Order as sent does not matter: ate-api-server sorts attributes by key before recording them.
