Attribute name (e.g. "architecture", "cpu_features", "sandbox_bundle_hash").

labels mirror the WorkerPool object's Kubernetes labels, which selectors match against. Kubernetes does not cap an object's label count, so the bound below is a generous guardrail, not a mirror of an upstream limit.

worker.epoch int64

epoch counts the runs of the worker pod's worker container: 1 for its first run and one more for each restart. 0 means it has not been reported.

A restarted worker has lost the sandboxes of the Actors it was hosting, so once epoch rises the control plane crashes every Actor placed during an earlier epoch; status.observed_epoch reports when that is done. It may only increase.

Output-only server-managed state. Absent from Create/Update request payloads; whatever a request carries here is ignored. A client moves state only through DrainWorker, MarkWorkerAvailable and MarkWorkerUnavailable, and the assignments are the scheduler's.

worker.status.state WorkerState
worker.status.capacity WorkerResources

The total resource capacity of the Worker.

A Worker should report every dimension of resources it has available to be consumed by Actors. Any resource not specified here is assumed to be 0. An Actor which requests a resource which is not present in a Worker's capacity will prevent that Actor from running on that Worker.

Shrinking capacity below allocated prevents new placements but does not evicts running Actors.

Resources match the Actor's definition of resources. They are matched by name and used for placement.

worker.status.capacity.resources.limits repeated Limits

limits is the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. Only "cpu" and "memory" are supported, each at most once, and each quantity must be greater than zero; the cpu limit must be less than 1000 cores.

worker.status.capacity.resources.limits.quantity string

worker.status.capacity.actors int32

worker.status.allocated WorkerResources

The allocated resources of the Worker. This is the sum of all the resources consumed by the Actors currently assigned to this Worker.

Capabilities

Capabilities adjusts a container's Linux capabilities relative to the default set. Drop applies first, then add, so a capability in both is granted. Capabilities are named without the "CAP_" prefix; "ALL" in drop removes the whole default set.

FieldDescriptionType
add

add lists capabilities to grant on top of the default set. "ALL" is rejected: name the individual capabilities the container needs.

 repeated string
drop

drop lists capabilities to remove from the default set. "ALL" drops the whole set, so drop+add expresses an exact set rather than a relative one.

 repeated string

Container

Container is a single application container of an ActorTemplate.

FieldDescriptionType
name string
image

image is the OCI image reference the container runs: [registry/]repository[:tag]@digest. Must be pinned by digest (e.g. "name@sha256:...").

 string
command

Entrypoint array; when set, the image's ENTRYPOINT and CMD are both ignored and the process argv is command + args. Unlike Kubernetes, $(VAR_NAME) references are NOT expanded.

 repeated string
args

Arguments to the entrypoint; the image's CMD is used if unset (unless command is set, which discards the image's CMD).

 repeated string
env

Env variables to set in the container's process environment. Unlike Kubernetes, $(VAR_NAME) references are NOT expanded in this field.

 repeated EnvVar
wakeup_probe

wakeup_probe gates each wakeup on this container: ResumeActor returns only after the probe answers HTTP 200. Without it, ResumeActor returns as soon as the container has started, which may be before it listens.

 WakeupProbe
volume_mounts

Keyed by mount_path: each path hosts exactly one mount, while a volume may be mounted at multiple paths.

 repeated VolumeMount
security_context

security_context adjusts the container's security settings. Unset leaves the default capability set.

 SecurityContext
resources

resources carries this container's compute limits, enforced inside the actor's sandbox. Only cpu and memory limits are supported.

CreateTagRequest

Request to tag the external snapshot a suspended Actor holds.

The tag captures whichever snapshot the Actor holds when the call runs. An Actor keeps no snapshot history — each suspend replaces the last — so a suspend that lands between taking a snapshot and tagging it moves what gets tagged. That race is inherent and accepted: the tag means "the Actor as of this call", not "the snapshot some earlier suspend returned".

The tag is given its own copy of that snapshot, so it survives the Actor being suspended again or deleted. To retry a create that failed or timed out, delete the tag first, which collects whatever that attempt stranded, and create it again.

FieldDescriptionType
tag

The tag to create. metadata.atespace, metadata.name, scope and source_actor are honored; metadata.atespace must match source_actor's, and status is ignored on write.

 Tag

CredentialHeader

CredentialHeader replaces the value of an HTTP request header with a credential. The Actor sends the header with a placeholder value, such as Authorization: <something>; the gateway discards that value and forwards the header with the credential instead. The placeholder itself is not inspected, so any value works. A request without the header is not modified.

FieldDescriptionType
header

The case-insensitive HTTP request header to replace when present.

 string
prefix

Prepended verbatim to the credential value. Include any desired separator; for example, use "Bearer " (including the space) for Authorization.

 string
credential_uri

Source-agnostic reference interpreted by a registered credential provider: ate-secret://<provider-class>/<provider-name>/<provider-specific-tail>

Exactly one of credential_uri and actor_jwt must be set.

 string
actor_jwt

A Substrate-issued JWT asserting the identity of the Actor that sent the request.

 ActorJwtSource

EgressRule

EgressRule allows traffic for a given protocol and destination (host name or IP, and port). The protocol fixes what the gateway matches on and when: a request, or a TLS connection at its ClientHello. Traffic that matches no rule is refused. All protocols here run over TCP; UDP is blocked. Protocols where the server sends first after connect are not supported.

Users should expect additional protocols to be supported in the future.

FieldDescriptionType
http

Cleartext HTTP to the named hosts: HTTP/1.1, and h2c as used by gRPC. TLS to these names is not allowed by this rule.

 HttpRule
https

HTTPS to the named hosts, intercepted (man-in-the-middle) so the gateway can authorize and modify each request. HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 inside the TLS connection; HTTP/3 is not supported.

 HttpsRule
tls_passthrough

TLS to the named servers, forwarded without decryption.

HttpRule

HttpRule allows cleartext HTTP and is evaluated per request on the request authority (Host or :authority) and port. The gateway resolves the name and dials it.

FieldDescriptionType
hostnames

Hostname patterns: a DNS name, or a DNS name with "*" as its leftmost label. The rule matches when any pattern matches.

The DNS name must conform to RFC 1034 and RFC 1123. It must be lowercase and must not have a trailing dot.

A wildcard replaces the complete leftmost label. ".example.com" matches exactly one non-empty label, such as "api.example.com". It does not match "example.com" or "nested.api.example.com". "" alone matches every name. No other wildcard syntax is accepted. A pattern without a wildcard matches only the complete normalized name. Patterns may overlap: the rule ranks by the most specific pattern that matches the destination.

Internationalized names must use their IDNA A-label (punycode) form; no Unicode conversion is performed. URLs, IP addresses, names with ports, malformed DNS names (for example, "foo..example.com"), and more than one trailing dot are invalid.

 repeated string
ports

Ports of the destination the Actor connected to. A port in a request's authority is neither matched nor dialed. Defaults to port 80.

 Ports
effects

Effects do not authorize traffic. They are applied only when this is the deciding rule.

 HttpRuleEffects

HttpRuleEffects

HttpRuleEffects contains effects applied by a matching HTTP or HTTPS rule.

FieldDescriptionType
replace_headers

Replaces placeholder request headers with credentials. A header is replaced only when the request from the Actor carries it; requests without the header are forwarded unchanged, so a credential reaches only the requests that ask for it. Header names must be unique case-insensitively.

Replacement is supported on HTTP and HTTPS. On HTTP, the gateway does not originate TLS to the destination. Without separate transport protection, observers can read the credential and attackers on the path can modify the request. Deployments may encrypt traffic outside the gateway; policy authors must account for any unprotected segments between credential injection and the intended destination.

 repeated CredentialHeader

HttpsRule

HttpsRule allows HTTPS that the gateway intercepts (MITM). Every Actor behind such a rule must trust the gateway CA. Without it, TLS to these names fails in the Actor.

A TLS connection whose SNI and port match is terminated with a leaf certificate for that name issued by the gateway CA. Each request inside it is then decided on its authority, and the gateway re-originates TLS to that authority; the SNI only selects the leaf.

Interception is for HTTP. A connection that sends no SNI does not match, and a non-HTTP protocol inside an intercepted connection fails.

FieldDescriptionType
hostnames

Server names matched against the SNI, in the pattern syntax of HttpRule.hostnames.

 repeated string
ports

Ports of the destination the Actor connected to. Defaults to port 443.

 Ports
effects

Effects do not authorize traffic. They are applied only when this is the deciding rule.

 HttpRuleEffects

MintActorJwtRequest

Request message for MintActorJwt.

FieldDescriptionType
actor

The actor for which the JWT should be issued.

Must be a valid actor that currently exists according to the actor store.

 ObjectRef

The audiences the minted JWT is bound to. Tokens are only issued with audience bindings, so at least one is required.

 repeated string
expiration_seconds

Lifetime of the JWT, in seconds.

 int64

MintActorJwtResponse

Response message for MintActorJwt.

FieldDescriptionType
actor_jwt

The signed actor JWT. Relying parties verify it with OpenID Connect Discovery against its issuer.

Claims:

  • iss: The issuer URL. Relying parties fetch <iss>/.well-known/openid-configuration to find the signing keys.
  • sub: actor/<atespace>/<name>.
  • aud: The requested audiences, always a JSON array.
  • exp, nbf, iat: Numeric Unix timestamps. nbf is five minutes before iat to allow for clock skew.
  • jti: A random token ID.
  • actor.ate.dev: A JSON object with the actor's atespace, actorName, and actorUID.

The subject and claim name say the token speaks for the actor itself. A token minted for a Substrate component acting on the actor's behalf (WorkerService.MintWorkerActorJwt) uses worker-for-actor in both places instead, so a relying party can grant the two different access.

 string
expire_time

expire_time is when actor_jwt expires. Equal to its exp claim.

TlsPassthroughRule

TlsPassthroughRule allows TLS that the gateway forwards without decryption. It is evaluated once per connection at the ClientHello, on the SNI and port, for any protocol carried over TLS. A connection that sends no SNI does not match. Protocols that upgrade to TLS after a cleartext exchange (STARTTLS) do not match. Because the gateway reads nothing after the ClientHello, a passthrough rule has no effects, and a policy change reaches an open connection only when it ends.

FieldDescriptionType
hostnames

Server names matched against the SNI, in the pattern syntax of HttpRule.hostnames.

 repeated string
ports

UpdateWorkerRequest

FieldDescriptionType
worker

The Worker to update. worker.metadata.name identifies which resource to update. atespace is always empty; Workers are global-scoped. worker.metadata.version and worker.metadata.uid are required preconditions.

labels is the only field an update may change. Every other field is replaced with what the request carries, and a field left unset is cleared — so read the Worker, change what you mean to change, and send the whole thing back. A request that alters an immutable field, by changing it or by omitting it, returns INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the field. status is output-only and whatever it carries is ignored.

VersionedSandboxCompat

VersionedSandboxCompat holds the compatibility schema version and the key-value compatibility attributes for a SandboxRuntime.

FieldDescriptionType
schema_version

Compatibility schema version (e.g. "v1") defining which runtime and hardware attributes are recorded and how they are computed.

 string
attributes

Key-value compatibility attributes defined by this schema version, covering both runtime assets (e.g. "sandbox_bundle_hash") and effective guest hardware features after masking (e.g. "architecture", "cpu_features"). Matched against a snapshot under the same schema_version: every attribute on the snapshot must be present on the worker with an equal value (except "cpu_features", where the snapshot's hexadecimal bitmask must be a bitwise subset of the worker's); keys only the worker has are ignored, so a worker can gain keys under one schema_version without invalidating older snapshots. Removing or recomputing a key is a new schema_version, under which older snapshots no longer match. Order as sent does not matter: ate-api-server sorts attributes by key before recording them.

 repeated AttributeEntry

A Worker should report every dimension of resources it has available to be consumed by Actors. Any resource not specified here is assumed to be 0. An Actor which requests a resource which is not present in a Worker's capacity will prevent that Actor from running on that Worker.

allocated

The allocated resources of the Worker. This is the sum of all the resources consumed by the Actors currently assigned to this Worker.

 WorkerResources
observed_epoch

observed_epoch is the latest epoch whose earlier Actors the control plane has crashed and released. While it is below epoch, Actors placed before the worker's last restart may still be reported as running.

 int64
default_runtime

Runtime that new and cold-booted actors start under, as reported by the Worker at registration. Snapshots matching default_runtime can also warm-boot on this worker.

 SandboxRuntime
restorable_runtimes

Additional runtimes (excluding default_runtime) that this worker can restore snapshots from right now.

GoldenSnapshotMode

GoldenSnapshotMode selects whether a template builds a golden snapshot.

ValueDescriptionNumber
GOLDEN_SNAPSHOT_MODE_UNSPECIFIED 0
GOLDEN_SNAPSHOT_MODE_ENABLED 1
GOLDEN_SNAPSHOT_MODE_DISABLED 2

SnapshotFidelity

SnapshotFidelity orders the state layers a snapshot can hold, lowest to highest. Each level includes the ones below it.

ValueDescriptionNumber
SNAPSHOT_FIDELITY_UNSPECIFIED 0
SNAPSHOT_FIDELITY_VOLUMES

Durable volumes only. The actor resumes by cold-booting its containers from the OCI image with the volumes restored.

 1
SNAPSHOT_FIDELITY_ROOTFS

Volumes plus the root filesystem changes made since boot. The actor cold-boots on resume with its rootfs writes back in place. Served by the micro-VM sandbox class only.

 2
SNAPSHOT_FIDELITY_MEMORY

Volumes, root filesystem changes, and process memory. The actor resumes where it left off.

 3

SnapshotStorageStatus

ValueDescriptionNumber

SNAPSHOT_STORAGE_STATUS_PENDING

 1

 2

TagScope

ValueDescriptionNumber

Not set and rejected wherever a client supplies a scope

 0
TAG_SCOPE_ATESPACE

 1

Published for use by Actors in any Atespace. The tag remains addressed through its owning Atespace.

WorkerState

ValueDescriptionNumber
WORKER_STATE_UNSPECIFIED 0
WORKER_STATE_ACTIVE

Ready; schedulable.

 1
WORKER_STATE_DRAINING

Pod terminating. Not schedulable. Final: a draining Worker never becomes active or unavailable again.

 2
WORKER_STATE_UNAVAILABLE

Registered but not Ready, or its the worker restarting. Not schedulable. Every Worker starts here until MarkWorkerAvailable.
